record.original_question: (V. M. Kopytov, N. Ya. Medvedev). Are there order automorphisms of Dlab groups that are not inner automorphisms?

evidence.quote: (V. M. Kopytov, N. Ya. Medvedev). Are there order automorphisms of Dlab groups that are not inner automorphisms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the real line and let $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be a closed interval of the extended real line. A Dlab group on $I$ is a group of order-preserving bijections of $I$ defined as follows. Fix an order-preserving bijection $\varphi:I\to I$ that has exactly two fixed points, namely the endpoints $a$ and $b$, and satisfies $\varphi(x)>x$ for all $x\in(a,b)$. The Dlab group $D(I,\varphi)$ is the group of all order-preserving bijections $g:I\to I$ such that $g$ fixes $a$ and $b$ and commutes with some integral power of $\varphi$ on a neighborhood of each interior point; equivalently, $D(I,\varphi)$ consists of those order automorphisms $g$ of $I$ for which there exist integers $m,n$ with $g\varphi^{m}=\varphi^{n}g$ on $I$. The group $D(I,\varphi)$ is a right-ordered (in fact lattice-ordered) group under the pointwise order inherited from $I$.

An order automorphism of a right-ordered group $(G,\le)$ is a group automorphism $\alpha:G\to G$ such that $\alpha(g)\ge e$ if and only if $g\ge e$, i.e.\ $\alpha$ preserves the positive cone. An automorphism is inner if it has the form $g\mapsto h g h^{-1}$ for some $h\in G$.

Question. Does there exist a Dlab group $D(I,\varphi)$ that admits an order automorphism which is not an inner automorphism?

Status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Dlab groups are constructed on a closed interval of an extended set of reals; certain Dlab groups DH*(I) and DH* lack normal relatively convex subgroups and have just two distinct linear orders.
status_evidence.claim: Defines Dlab groups but does not resolve the order-automorphism question.
